I'll just pass the spine chain directly as the sweep source, using an ellipse radius function for the body profile, then extend the path slightly to cover the rump and chest regions beyond the joints.

For the neck, I'm setting up a separate chain parented to the chest tip, running from chest to a neck midpoint to the head base, then sweeping that chain too. The head joint attaches at the end of this neck chain, parented to its final segment.

For the head itself, I'm planning a wide-cheeked skull region with a muzzle, nose, tall fox-like ears, and decal eyes styled as kitsune-like amber-crimson irises, plus cheek ruff fur and a separately jointed lower jaw.

I want to position everything relative to the head joint using local forward/up/left offsets so it stays independent of roll, so I'm setting up a small helper function for that convenience.

For most parts I'm using simple sphere geometries scaled along each axis rather than orienting them, since the head faces roughly forward and world-aligned axes should work fine for this stylized look.

Now I'm working out the kitsune's color palette: cream-white fur with soft lavender cel-shading, vermilion markings on the face, dark ear tips with pink insides, and nine tails fading from white to pale gold with blue spirit-flame tips.

For accessories and base, I'm planning a shimenawa rope with shide paper and a gold bell around the neck, plus floating foxfire orbs. Tuning each tail's length based on its position in the fan, with central tails slightly longer than outer ones, and checking the geometry stays clear of the lanterns while adding small z-offset alternation between tails to prevent them from overlapping.

Each tail is built as a catmull-rom chain of three joints, with nine tails giving 27 joints total, named sequentially so defaults produce something like tail01, tail02, etc.
